note: Exact target: Let p be a prime and G a finite group of order p^n, n>=1; prove p divides |Z(G)| and hence Z(G) has a nonidentity element. Direct mechanism: conjugation action partitions G; fixed singleton orbits are exactly Z(G); every noncentral orbit has size [G:C_G(x)], a nontrivial divisor of p^n, hence divisible by p. Therefore |G|-|Z(G)| is divisible by p. Since p divides |G|, p divides |Z(G)|; as p>=2 and identity lies in Z(G), divisibility forces |Z(G)|>=p and gives a nonidentity element.
